CA-9-Q1.rationale: CA-9-A.4 sets the auto-admission gate at candidate_rank_score ≥ 0.70 using the Locked Rule 18 formula, aligning with the median of current adapters in §8. This keeps admission consistent with the canonical ranking math and the bootstrap baselines referenced in `docs/specs/ORCHESTRA_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md` §4.3.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: CA-9-B.1 explicitly amends §25 Locked Rule 2 from 25 → 26 to add Agent #26 (Orchestra Research Agent) and updates the §15.1 roster partition. This is necessary for the auto-admission pipeline owned by Agent #26 per CA-9-A and CA-9-B.5.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: Splitting the write-path into an executor mirrors §15.5 EXECUTOR_REGISTRY and its validator invariant M3 (auto_write_internal must pair with requires_human_gate), as already done for the Self-Renewal Executor in CA-7. This avoids changing BaseAgent.guard() semantics for primary agents (CA-9-B.6) while keeping Agent #26 recommend_only for research.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: Promoting CA-9-A + CA-9-B first de-risks the path since CA-9-C depends on Agent #10 Monitor (DORMANT in §15.1 row 10) and new topics like `10.customer.issue.v1`. It also cleanly sequences with CA-10, which further formalizes the customer-signal plumbing into ProductSSOT.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: CA-10-A.2 defines one ProductSSOT per (productId, environment) aligning with §16.3's dev/prd dual deployment, making it a universal living record. Mandating creation at ProductRegistry insertion ensures consistent context for §4/§6/§9 consumption per CA-10-D.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: CA-10-A.4 amends §7 to add the ProductSSOT update as item #5 and makes the run atomic with Self-Protect rollback (§10) if the write fails. This preserves data integrity and keeps the Output Contract cohesive across URL, delta, and SSOT state.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: Per CA-10-D.2, admin annotations/overrides are CEO-equivalent directives for that product, so admin override should prevail and auto-gen entries be flagged `overridden=true`. Governance traceability remains intact via §14.2 hash-chained version history in CA-10-C.3.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: Promoting A+B+C first lands the entity, auto-updates, and human layer while deferring CA-10-D (symbiotic loop across §4/§6/§9) and CA-10-E (retention/portability tying into §14.3) to reduce operational risk. This sequencing matches the engineering impact summary’s layering.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Sequencing CA-9 (A+B) and CA-10 (A+B+C) before their tightly coupled parts reduces drift with §15.5 EXECUTOR_REGISTRY and §14.3 retention. Several picks intentionally propose canonical amendments that must pass the CA-n cycle per §18.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: The 0.70 threshold aligns with the median wired-adapter rank scores documented in §4.3 of the Orchestra Integration Spec, specifically matching the range of existing members like claude-code (0.85), v0 (0.85), and browserless (0.85). This threshold ensures new members meet the quality bar of current Orchestra members while allowing room for innovation, as noted in CA-9-A.4's reference to the 0.65-0.92 spread of existing adapters.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: Adding Agent #26 as a primary agent with its own roster slot is appropriate given its unique role in Orchestra self-expansion per CA-9-B.5, which requires always-on monitoring and auto-admission capabilities distinct from existing agents. The amendment to Locked Rule 2 from 25 to 26 agents maintains the canonical partition structure (13 embedded + 8 FlowAI-internal + 5 Ops Runners) while properly categorizing Agent #26 as embedded, consistent with its charter to operate across all products.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: Requiring `requires_human_gate` alongside the dual-authority declaration follows the established pattern from CA-7's Self-Renewal Executor (§15.5 EXECUTOR_REGISTRY) and provides an additional safety layer for auto-write operations. This approach is consistent with CA-7 Mitigation M3, which mandates that any `auto_write_internal` authority must be paired with `requires_human_gate`, ensuring human oversight remains available even for automated Orchestra admission decisions.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: Promoting all three sub-amendments together is optimal because they form a coherent system: CA-9-A defines the auto-admission mechanism, CA-9-B provides the necessary agent infrastructure (Agent #26 and charter expansions for #11, #15, #17), and CA-9-C closes the customer feedback loop into Self-Renewal. The interdependencies are explicit in CA-9-B.6's reference to shared BaseAgent.guard() amendments with CA-7, making partial promotion risk incomplete functionality.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: Mandatory ProductSSOT for every product aligns with the CEO-locked feature spec's vision of replacing manual documentation entirely per product, as stated in CA-10-A.1. The atomic inclusion in the Output Contract (§7 amendment in CA-10-A.4) ensures data integrity by making ProductSSOT updates part of the transactional boundary, preventing orphaned runs without corresponding documentation updates.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: Atomic ProductSSOT updates as part of the Output Contract ensure the strongest data integrity, as noted in CA-10-A.4's specification that runs failing to update ProductSSOT are considered INCOMPLETE and rolled back. This strictness aligns with the existing Self-Protect snapshot + Self-Heal pattern from §10, maintaining consistency with FlowAI's governance model where all outputs must meet completeness criteria.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: Admin overrides should always win per CA-10-D.2's explicit statement that 'human annotations and overrides are treated as CEO-equivalent directives for that product's pipeline run.' This maintains the human-in-the-loop authority model consistent with §10.2's Human Gates and ensures that admin decisions about issue severity or other safety signals are respected across pipeline runs, with new auto-generated entries flagged as `overridden=true`.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: Promoting all five sub-amendments together maximizes system value as explicitly stated in CA-10's disposition request: 'the system value scales superlinearly with completeness — overrides without a feed-back loop are documentation; the feed-back loop without overrides is automation without checks.' The coherent design spans from entity definition (A) through symbiotic feedback (D) to GDPR compliance (E), with CA-10-B's integration with CA-7's Self-Renewal Executor providing the necessary write paths.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Both amendments demonstrate strong alignment with existing SSOT patterns, particularly the human-in-the-loop governance model and the metadata-driven architecture from §3.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: The 0.70 threshold is appropriate as it matches the median wired-adapter rank score, ensuring that only high-quality candidates are admitted. This threshold also aligns with the bootstrap baselines in the Orchestra Integration Spec.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: Amending Locked Rule 2 to include Agent #26 is necessary to maintain the canonical roster of 26 unique agent IDs. This amendment is crucial for the proper functioning of the Orchestra Research Agent.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: The dual-authority charter for Agent #26 is reasonable, as it allows for both recommend_only and auto_write_internal capabilities. This setup ensures that the agent can perform its duties effectively while maintaining the integrity of the system.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: Promoting all three sub-amendments A, B, and C together is essential for creating a coherent capability. This approach ensures that the Orchestra can evolve autonomously and that customer-driven self-renewal is effectively managed.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: Making ProductSSOT mandatory for every product ensures consistency and data integrity across all products managed by FlowAI. This approach eliminates the risk of opt-out and ensures that all products benefit from the living document feature.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: Including ProductSSOT in the Output Contract as a mandatory step ensures that the ProductSSOT update is atomic with the run output. This strictness guarantees data integrity and consistency, aligning with the overall goals of the system.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: Admin overrides should always take precedence to ensure that human directives are respected. This approach aligns with the principle of treating annotations and overrides as CEO-equivalent directives, maintaining the integrity of the system.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: Promoting all five sub-amendments together ensures that the ProductSSOT feature is complete and coherent. This approach provides a living document per product, auto-maintained and human-augmentable, with a symbiotic feed-back loop into the pipeline.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The amendments in CA-9 and CA-10 introduce significant changes to the SSOT, including the expansion of the Orchestra and the introduction of ProductSSOT. These changes are crucial for the evolution and maintenance of the system, ensuring that it remains robust and adaptable to new requirements and feedback.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: The 0.70 threshold is a reasonable balance between inclusivity and quality, ensuring that only capable candidates are admitted while allowing for a diverse range of tools to be integrated into the Orchestra. This threshold aligns with the median rank score of existing wired adapters, maintaining the quality standard of the Orchestra.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: Approving the amendment to Locked Rule 2 to include Agent #26 as the 26th agent is necessary for the effective implementation of the auto-admission mechanism. This change ensures that the Orchestra can dynamically evolve without manual intervention, which is crucial for maintaining the system's adaptability and efficiency.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: The dual-authority charter for Agent #26, which includes both 'recommend_only' and 'auto_write_internal' authorities, is essential for enabling the agent to perform its functions effectively. The 'auto_write_internal' authority is necessary for the agent to update the Orchestra registry during the auto-admission process, while the 'recommend_only' authority ensures that the agent's actions are subject to human oversight when necessary.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: Promoting all three sub-amendments (A, B, and C) together ensures the coherent and comprehensive implementation of the auto-admission mechanism, customer feedback loop, and the necessary agent charter expansions. This approach avoids fragmentation and ensures that all related changes are integrated simultaneously, maintaining the system's consistency and functionality.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: Making the ProductSSOT mandatory for every product ensures consistency and standardization across all products managed by FlowAI. This approach eliminates the risk of inconsistent documentation and ensures that all products benefit from the living document feature, which is crucial for maintaining the system's reliability and traceability.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: Including the ProductSSOT update in the Output Contract as a mandatory and atomic operation ensures data integrity and consistency. This approach guarantees that every pipeline run that produces an output also updates the ProductSSOT, maintaining a complete and accurate record of all changes and actions related to the product. The atomic nature of the update ensures that any failure in the ProductSSOT update process results in a rollback, preventing partial or incomplete updates.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: Prioritizing admin overrides ensures that human directives are respected and maintained in the system. This approach aligns with the principle of human-in-the-loop oversight, ensuring that admin decisions are not overridden by automated processes without explicit intervention. The 'overridden=true' flag provides transparency and traceability, allowing stakeholders to understand the context and rationale behind admin overrides.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: Promoting all five sub-amendments (A, B, C, D, and E) together ensures the comprehensive and coherent implementation of the ProductSSOT feature. This approach integrates the foundational entity, auto-update mechanisms, human-editable layer, symbiotic feedback loop, and retention policies, creating a robust and functional living document system for each product managed by FlowAI. This holistic implementation avoids fragmentation and ensures that all related changes are integrated simultaneously, maintaining the system's consistency and reliability.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: The 0.70 threshold is appropriate as it matches the median wired-adapter rank score, ensuring that new members are of a similar quality. This threshold also allows for some experimentation, as members with a rank score of 0.60-0.70 can still be admitted, but with a lower rank score multiplier of 0.5 during the Trial state.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: Adding Agent #26 as a new primary agent in EMBEDDED_AGENTS is the most straightforward solution, as it does not require any changes to the existing code or architecture. It also ensures that the agent is discoverable and can be easily referenced in other parts of the system.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: The dual-authority charter `[recommend_only, auto_write_internal]` is safe and appropriate for Agent #26, as it allows the agent to write to the Orchestra registry on auto-admission while still requiring human approval for other actions. This approach provides a balance between automation and human oversight, ensuring that critical decisions are not made without human input.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: Promoting all three sub-amendments together is recommended, as they form a coherent capability that is more valuable when implemented as a whole. Splitting them up could lead to inconsistencies and potential issues with integration, as the capabilities are designed to work together.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: Making ProductSSOT mandatory for every product ensures that all products have a living document that accumulates history across runs and is fed back into the next pipeline run. This provides a consistent and reliable source of information for both the system and human users, and helps to ensure data integrity and consistency across the platform.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: Adopting the proposed strictness for the ProductSSOT inclusion in the Output Contract is recommended, as it ensures that the system maintains data integrity and consistency. If the ProductSSOT write fails, rolling back the entire run ensures that the system remains in a consistent state and that no partial or incomplete data is stored.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: Admin override always winning is the most appropriate solution, as it ensures that human input is respected and that the system does not override human decisions without explicit approval. This approach also provides a clear audit trail, as new auto-gen entries are flagged `overridden=true` referencing the override, making it easy to track and understand the decision-making process.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: Promoting all five sub-amendments together is recommended, as they form a coherent capability that is more valuable when implemented as a whole. Splitting them up could lead to inconsistencies and potential issues with integration, as the capabilities are designed to work together.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The CA-9 and CA-10 amendments are well-designed and address important gaps in the system. The proposed changes are coherent and build upon existing capabilities, ensuring that the system remains consistent and reliable. The amendments also provide a balance between automation and human oversight, which is crucial for maintaining data integrity and ensuring that critical decisions are not made without human input.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: CA-9-A.4 explicitly defines the auto-admission threshold as 0.70 rank_score, matching the median wired adapter (e.g., claude-code at 0.85). This aligns with Locked Rule 18's ranking formula (§8) and avoids redundant coverage via the capability-gap rule.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: CA-9-B.1 proposes amending Locked Rule 2 from 25 to 26 agents to accommodate Agent #26. The validator in BaseAgent.js (§15.1) will enforce this new partition (13 embedded + 8 FlowAI-only + 5 Ops Runners), preserving the roster lock invariant.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: CA-9-B.5 approves Agent #26's dual authority (recommend_only + auto_write_internal) without requiring requires_human_gate. This leverages the BaseAgent.guard() extension per CA-9-B.6, inherited from Self-Renewal Executor spec §4.2 (commit 446ddb5), ensuring per-invocation authority checks.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: CA-9 states that sub-amendments A, B, and C form a single coherent capability (Orchestra evolution + feedback loop). Promoting them together avoids drift risks, as CA-9-B's Agent #26 and CA-9-C's customer signals are interdependent per the combined disposition rationale.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: CA-10-A.2 mandates ProductSSOT creation on first product registration, with no opt-out. This ensures consistency across all products per CA-10's design, aligning with §13 RLS policies and eliminating documentation gaps for providers.

CA-10-Q2.rationale: CA-10-A.4 amends §7 to make ProductSSOT updates atomic with output delivery. Failure triggers rollback via §10 Self-Protect, ensuring data integrity. This strictness prevents incomplete runs, per CA-10's tamper-evident versioning (CA-10-C.3).

CA-10-Q3.rationale: CA-10-C.4 and CA-10-D.2 prioritize admin overrides as CEO-equivalent directives. Conflicting auto-gen entries are flagged overridden=true, preserving the override's authority. This respects human judgment while maintaining audit trails via §14 GovernanceAuditLog.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: CA-10's sub-amendments A-E form a symbiotic loop (auto-documentation + feedback). Promoting together ensures coherence: CA-10-D's pipeline integration relies on CA-10-A's entity, and CA-10-C's human layer balances automation. Deferring any part risks fragmentation.

CA-9-Q1.rationale: CA-9-A.4 sets the auto-admission threshold at `candidate_rank_score ≥ 0.70`, and the draft explicitly says this matches the median wired-adapter baseline from `docs/specs/ORCHESTRA_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md` §4.3. I would keep that floor because CA-9-A.5's Trial/Probation lifecycle already provides the quality-control buffer after admission.

CA-9-Q3.rationale: CA-9-B.1 is explicit that adding Agent #26 requires amending Locked Rule 2 from 25 to 26 unique agent IDs, and §15.1 / §15.2 are updated to include the new roster slot and topics. The draft treats Agent #26 as a primary agent, not an executor, so reshaping it into CA-7-style EXECUTOR_REGISTRY would contradict the stated design.

CA-9-Q4.rationale: CA-9-B.5 proposes `[recommend_only, auto_write_internal]`, but CA-7's EXECUTOR_REGISTRY precedent and CA-9-B.6 both emphasize that auto-write paths should be paired with `requires_human_gate` when internal writes are authorized. Requiring the gate preserves the dual-authority model while narrowing the blast radius of Agent #26's registry updates.

CA-9-Q8.rationale: The draft repeatedly frames CA-9-A, CA-9-B, and CA-9-C as one coherent capability, and CA-9-C depends on the customer-feedback path that feeds Self-Renewal while CA-9-B supplies Agent #26 for discovery and expansion. Promoting them together also aligns with the combined disposition request and avoids landing partial orchestration without its enabling agents and topic wiring.

CA-10-Q1.rationale: CA-10-A.1 and CA-10-A.4 make ProductSSOT a canonical per-product living document, and the draft says it should be auto-created at `ProductRegistry` insertion time. CA-10-Q2.rationale: CA-10-A.4 is unambiguous that the ProductSSOT write is atomic with the rest of the output contract, and a run that fails to update ProductSSOT is considered incomplete and rolled back. This is reinforced by CA-10-B.3 and CA-10-B.4, which treat Clearance and Human Gate events as governance-record writes rather than best-effort side effects.

CA-10-Q3.rationale: CA-10-D.2 explicitly says human annotations and overrides are treated as CEO-equivalent directives for that product's pipeline run, so admin override should remain authoritative. The draft's override mechanism in CA-10-C.4 also models overrides as append-only replacements that future runs must respect rather than automatically supersede.

CA-10-Q7.rationale: CA-10-A through CA-10-E are tightly coupled: the entity, auto-update triggers, human-editable layer, symbiotic feed-back loop, and retention/export rules are designed to operate as one system. The draft itself recommends sequencing all of CA-7, CA-8, CA-9, and CA-10 in the same cycle, and CA-10-D explicitly depends on ProductSSOT being present before the pipeline runs.
